notes: Cuyahoga County's public hospital system, governed by a county-appointed board; almost 9,000 employees as of December 2023 and the 10th largest employer in Northeast Ohio. Not a business; grant was $10M in FY2022 and FY2024.

Single-purpose 501(c)(3) that raised money for the 2016 Republican National Convention in Cleveland; revenue of $34.2M (2014), $7.4M (2015) and $16.3M (2016), then wound down to zero by 2018. Its 990s list a handful of officers (David Gilbert, Jon Pinney) and no large staff, so the bucket is a floor from the filings rather than a stated headcount.

parent: Transportation Research Center Inc. (affiliate of The Ohio State University)
notes: TRC Inc. is a 501(c)(3) affiliated with Ohio State that operates the East Liberty proving grounds on Honda-owned land under a 1988 management agreement; Wikipedia says more than 400 employees, JobsOhio's own report shows 347 retained jobs, and its Form 5500 counted 454-471 participants in 2015-2023. Auto class said business; the grants were $9M of R&D money for the SMART Center, so a reader may ask whether this is really a university or Honda project.

The Research Institute is a 501(c)(3) arm of Nationwide Children's Hospital in Columbus, which reports about 11,900 employees. ProPublica lists the EIN under 'Nationwide Childrens Hospital Inc (Research Institute At Nationwide)'.

parent: altafiber (Cincinnati Bell Inc.), owned by Macquarie Infrastructure Partners; Digital Access Ohio is its joint venture with JobsOhio
notes: Digital Access Ohio LLC was formed in 2022 by Canton-based Agile Networks with JobsOhio committing up to $40M; altafiber (Cincinnati Bell) bought Agile on May 2, 2022 for $65.5M, and its FY2022 10-K calls DAO 'our Joint Venture with the State of Ohio', carries the JobsOhio money as a 'Digital Access Ohio Advance' and reports about 5,800 employees at December 31, 2022. Cincinnati Bell itself has been owned by Macquarie's Red Fiber Parent LLC since September 2021, so JobsOhio's grants flowed into a JV it co-owns with a PE-held telecom, not a small business.

County economic development corporation and JobsOhio network partner (via OhioSE) in South Point; its 990s list three key staff (Bill Dingus, Jeremy Clay, Jesse Layne) and revenue of $3.6M-$14.3M a year in 2018-2024. Grants were revitalization and spec-building (OSIP) money for The Point industrial park, not an operating business.

CoverMyMeds was founded in Twinsburg in 2008 and bought by McKesson in January 2017 for $1.1B (about 450 employees then), before the first grant year; McKesson's FY2020 10-K reports about 80,000 employees. McKesson moved its HQ from San Francisco, CA to Irving, TX effective April 1, 2019, so the FY2017 grant was under a CA parent and the 2019-2022 grants under a TX parent.

Public company (NASDAQ: FSLR) headquartered in Tempe, AZ; FY2020 10-K reports approximately 5,100 associates as of December 31, 2020. Its predecessor Solar Cells Inc. started in Toledo, but the parent was formed in Arizona in 1999 and the Ohio plants in Perrysburg and Lake Township are subsidiaries.

Nestlé Purina PetCare (St. Louis, MO) is a wholly owned division of Nestlé S.A. of Vevey, Switzerland, which employs roughly 270,000-275,000 people; the JobsOhio release says Nestlé alone had 3,300 Ohio employees when it announced the $550M Williamsburg Township plant. The EDGAR match is the legacy Ralston Purina registrant, not a current filer.

JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (Columbus-chartered) is the main bank subsidiary of JPMorgan Chase & Co., New York; the FY2019 10-K reports headcount of 256,981 and JobsOhio's 2018 release puts its central Ohio workforce at 19,200. The EDGAR match to 'Warehouse Funding Avery Point VII' is a trust filing under the bank's EIN, not the parent.

British Airways has been a wholly owned subsidiary of IAG since 2011; IAG is registered in Madrid, Spain with corporate headquarters in London and about 76,000 employees. The FY2024 payment is an Air Service Restoration Program route incentive for the CVG-London Heathrow flight that began June 2023, not a site project.

parent: Yorkville Intermodal Terminals LLC (Charles J. Betters and Victor DiGeronimo)
notes: Project LLC formed December 2016 (Ohio charter 3965739) by Aliquippa, PA developer Charles J. Betters (C.J. Betters Enterprises) with Cleveland's Victor DiGeronimo (Independence Excavating) to buy and clean up the former Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel mill in Yorkville for a barge terminal; a 2024 Jefferson County Port Authority report still calls it an ownership group marketing the site. The LLC itself has no staff; the owners' companies are private and no source gives their size, so the bucket reflects the LLC only.

Privately held, Epprecht family-controlled cheese packer headquartered in Hiram with employees holding a 20% ESOP stake; a February 2020 presentation put the Hiram plant at more than 500 workers and the new headquarters at 253, its Form 5500 counted 3,507 participants in 2019 (4,879 by 2023), and JobsOhio shows 671 retained jobs on the $5.1M grant. Company-wide it sat under 5,000 in 2020-2021 but is close to that line now.

Honda of America Mfg., Inc. (Marysville, Anna and East Liberty plants) was the U.S. manufacturing subsidiary of Tokyo-based Honda Motor Co., which employed roughly 200,000 people worldwide in 2015-2016 (194,173 in 2025); JobsOhio shows 2,520 retained jobs on the Anna engine plant project. In 2020 the entity was folded into Honda Development & Manufacturing of America, LLC.

parent: Jefferis Real Estate, LLC (T.J. and John Jefferis Sr.)
notes: Family real-estate developer founded in Barnesville in 2001 by brothers T.J. and John Jefferis Sr.; by 2018 it had built nine leased industrial buildings in Barnesville-area industrial parks, mostly for oil and gas tenants employing over 400 people, and JobsOhio's June 2018 report shows a $5M Revitalization Grant against $6.4M of investment and zero direct jobs. No headcount is published; a two-owner developer of this kind is very likely under 100 employees, and the 400 jobs belong to tenants, not to Jefferis.

Private, family-controlled medical and dental equipment maker founded in Versailles in 1915 with corporate offices in Miamisburg (Dayton area); the JobsOhio release on the Versailles expansion cites nearly 2,000 employees worldwide, 1,002 retained and 99 new jobs, and its Form 5500 shows 1,678 participants in 2019.

Andelyn is a for-profit gene-therapy contract manufacturer spun out of Nationwide Children's clinical manufacturing group in 2020 and wholly owned by the hospital, which has about 11,900 employees; Andelyn itself committed 170 jobs and JobsOhio gave a $5M R&D Center Grant plus a Growth Fund loan for its 185,000 sq ft Columbus plant. On its own Andelyn would be 100-499; the bucket follows the ultimate parent rule.

parent: Ensemble Health Partners (majority owned by Golden Gate Capital from August 2019; founded by Bon Secours Mercy Health)
notes: Cincinnati (Blue Ash) hospital revenue-cycle firm founded 2014 by Mercy Health; Golden Gate Capital took a majority stake on August 1, 2019 and the September 2021 S-1 reports 6,492 full-time employees as of June 30, 2021 with principal offices at 11511 Reed Hartman Highway, Cincinnati. At the first grant year it was smaller (3,600 employees in May 2019 per the Golden Gate deal coverage), so the bucket reflects the later grant years; the IPO was pulled and Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners bought in during 2022.

parent: Ohio-West Virginia Excavating Co. (Dennis Hendershot and Roger Lewis)
notes: Shadyside excavating contractor run by Dennis Hendershot and Roger Lewis that owned the largest tract of the 500-acre Dilles Bottom site beside FirstEnergy's Burger plant, which JobsOhio's 2015 Revitalization Grants ($3M plus $277,275) helped prepare for PTT Global Chemical's proposed ethane cracker; the cracker was never built. No source gives a headcount; it bids roughly $1M municipal jobs, so 100-499 is a guess between a small local contractor and a mid-size one, and the grant really paid for site work, hence site_development.

Honda Development & Manufacturing of America, LLC (Raymond/Marysville) is the 2020 merger of Honda's North American manufacturing and R&D subsidiaries, wholly owned by Tokyo-based Honda Motor Co. with roughly 200,000 employees worldwide; JobsOhio shows 8,023 retained jobs and $232M of total commitments, most of it the 2022 EV and battery package. The EIN predates the LLC (it was Honda R&D Americas' EIN), which is why grants appear under it in 2019.
